Container.Name: tape
Container.Overview: Tape — Schwab-backed market + account data tier for CEF Tracker + Keystone. ONE neutral template for dev and prod: at creation set Name (tape / tape-dev), image tag (:stable for prod, :dev for dev), network + a static IP if you use one, the discrete DB_* vars pointing at the tape-db container, and the SCHWAB_CALLBACK_URL for this env. The app assembles the DB connection string from DB_HOST/DB_PORT/DB_USER/DB_PASSWORD/DB_NAME (§2 B.10) — no baked DATABASE_URL.
Container.Description: Tape — Schwab-backed market + account data tier (one neutral template, dev+prod).

Config.Name: HTTP Port
Config.Description: App HTTP port

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Encrypted token store. REQUIRED - set an absolute path on a POOL (e.g. /mnt/<pool>/appdata/tape/data, or .../tape-dev/data for a dev container). Do NOT leave it blank and do not point it at the RAM-backed root filesystem. The retrievable ops/error logs also default to a subdirectory of this mount.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: Where the scheduled pg_dump lands. REQUIRED for a real backup: WITHOUT this mount the dump is written INSIDE the container and destroyed by the next update — the job still reports success, which is why it went unnoticed for months. Set an absolute path on a POOL DIFFERENT from the one holding the DB container's data (e.g. /mnt/<other-pool>/appdata/tape/backups), so one pool failure cannot take both the warehouse and its only backup. The app WARNS (ntfy) at boot and at every dump if this path is not a persistent mount. ⚠️ THIS MOUNT IS THE BACKUP_DIR SETTING — there is deliberately no BACKUP_DIR Variable, because the two must never disagree: a Variable pointing anywhere other than this mount point would send dumps into the container filesystem, which is the exact silent failure above.

Config.Name: Shared alerting config
Config.Description: READ-ONLY mount of the shared fleet config directory — set the host path to the directory holding configs/alerting.env (EMAIL_TO, EMAIL_FROM, SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD). THIS MOUNT IS THE EMAIL ALERT CHANNEL: the SMTP settings are deliberately read from that file at send time and NEVER from the environment, because an environment variable is visible to anyone who can run a container inspect and the SMTP password is a real credential. Without this mount the email channel is skipped and only ntfy alerts — and with neither configured, every alert this service raises goes NOWHERE (it says so loudly in the boot log). One file serves the whole fleet, so rotating the password or moving the inbox is one edit rather than one per container.

Config.Name: SCHWAB_APP_KEY
Config.Description: Schwab app key

Config.Name: SCHWAB_APP_SECRET
Config.Description: Schwab app secret

Config.Name: SCHWAB_CALLBACK_URL
Config.Description: OAuth callback URL for THIS env — e.g. https://tape.your-domain.example/v1/admin/callback (prod) or https://tape-dev.your-domain.example/v1/admin/callback (dev). REQUIRED: the image carries no default and it must match the URI registered on the Schwab app.

Config.Name: TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY
Config.Description: Fernet key for token-at-rest encryption

Config.Name: TOKEN_STORE_PATH
Config.Description: Where the encrypted Schwab token file lives INSIDE the container. Must sit under the /data mount above or it does not survive a container recreate — and losing it means re-running the consent flow by hand. Leave at the default unless you have a reason.

Config.Name: REAUTH_MAX_CONSENT_AGE_HOURS
Config.Description: Tripwire for the re-auth bot going quiet. Schwab's refresh token dies 168h (7 days) after consent and the bot re-consents about every 72h, so 120h alerts with roughly 48h of runway left while still tolerating one delayed bot cycle. Raising this past ~150 leaves no time to act before the feeds stop.

Config.Name: DB_HOST
Config.Description: Warehouse DB host - the address of the tape-db container serving THIS environment

Config.Name: DB_PORT
Config.Description: Warehouse DB port

Config.Name: DB_USER
Config.Description: Warehouse DB user (matches the tape-db container's POSTGRES_USER)

Config.Name: DB_PASSWORD
Config.Description: Warehouse DB password (matches the tape-db container's POSTGRES_PASSWORD)

Config.Name: DB_NAME
Config.Description: Warehouse DB name (matches the tape-db container's POSTGRES_DB)

Config.Name: DATABASE_URL
Config.Description: OPTIONAL override — full SQLAlchemy URL (postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host:port/db). Leave BLANK to use the discrete DB_* vars above; if set, it wins.

Config.Name: DB_POOL_SIZE
Config.Description: Persistent SQLAlchemy connections. The parallel backfill drain holds one per worker across its HTTP calls, so too small a pool makes ordinary API reads queue behind a nightly drain. Raising this means also checking the DB server's own max_connections — PostgreSQL defaults to 100 and this is not its only client.

Config.Name: DB_MAX_OVERFLOW
Config.Description: Extra connections allowed above DB_POOL_SIZE at peak, returned to the pool afterwards.

Config.Name: DB_POOL_RESERVE
Config.Description: Connections the background drain must leave for everything else — the API's own reads, the scheduler, the census. This is what stops a maxed-out backfill from making a consumer request wait on it.

Config.Name: NTFY_URL
Config.Description: Full ntfy topic URL for alerts (e.g. https://ntfy.sh/<your-topic>); blank = log-only. This is where Tape shouts about things that need a human — chiefly the 7-day Schwab refresh token approaching its lapse, after which the data feeds stop until someone re-runs the consent flow. Log-only is a supported posture and the same warning stays readable at GET /v1/admin/token/detail, but nothing will page you. Treat the topic URL as a capability: anyone who knows it can read your alerts and post to them, so choose an unguessable topic name.

Config.Name: BACKUP_ENABLED
Config.Description: Master switch for the nightly pg_dump. Setting this false ALSO unregisters the freshness watchdog, so nothing is left watching for a missing dump — which is correct (a watchdog for a job you switched off would page forever about an absence you chose) but worth knowing before you flip it.

Config.Name: BACKUP_TIME
Config.Description: WHEN the nightly dump starts — a 24-hour HH:MM wall-clock time in BACKUP_TIMEZONE below. Choose a slot that fits around whatever copies the dump offsite: the dump is a long heavy read, and running it while the offsite tool is reading the same disk makes them fight. ⛔ THIS ONE FAILS CLOSED, unlike every other setting here. Blank or unparseable means NO dump is scheduled at all and the service pages you urgently at boot saying so — it will NOT quietly fall back to a default hour, because a dump at a guessed time is worse than a dump that visibly did not run. The freshness watchdog keeps running through that refusal, so the growing absence is reported daily as well. Accepts HH:MM only: no AM/PM, no seconds, no timezone suffix (the zone is the separate Variable below).

Config.Name: BACKUP_TIMEZONE
Config.Description: The IANA timezone BACKUP_TIME is expressed in. DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE: the market jobs run on Eastern because the exchange session defines them, but the backup is not a market job — its slot is set by your host's offsite pipeline, which you think about in your own local time. Changing one no longer moves the other. Must be a full zone NAME such as America/Chicago or Europe/London — NOT an abbreviation like CST (ambiguous) and NOT a fixed offset like UTC-6 (it would not follow daylight saving, so the dump would drift an hour twice a year). Leaving this BLANK is safe and simply uses the default above — unlike BACKUP_TIME, this one is optional and behaves optionally. An UNKNOWN zone name is different: that is a wrong answer rather than no answer, so it refuses to schedule the dump rather than silently falling back to UTC and moving the slot by hours.

Config.Name: BACKUP_KEEP_DAILY
Config.Description: How many recent dumps to keep on this disk. The dumps are UNCOMPRESSED so an external snapshot tool can deduplicate them day over day, which makes each one full-size — check the pool has room before raising this. ⛔ BACKUP_KEEP_DAILY, _WEEKLY and _MONTHLY must not ALL be zero: the pruner would then delete every dump including the one it just wrote, so the app refuses to start. Use BACKUP_ENABLED=false if you want no backups; do not empty the retention.

Config.Name: BACKUP_KEEP_WEEKLY
Config.Description: Older weekly generations to keep locally. ZERO ON PURPOSE: the offsite copy holds the long-term history, so this disk's job is a week of FAST recovery points rather than an archive, and keeping the long tail in both places pays for the same history twice. Only raise this if nothing external is copying BACKUP_DIR elsewhere — in which case your total history really is BACKUP_KEEP_DAILY days and nothing more.

Config.Name: BACKUP_KEEP_MONTHLY
Config.Description: Older monthly generations to keep locally. Zero for the same reason as the weekly tier above.

Config.Name: BACKUP_MAX_AGE_HOURS
Config.Description: How stale the newest dump ON DISK may get before the freshness watchdog pages. This alarm reads the actual directory, which is what makes it different from the job-level one: a dump can run, report success honestly, and still leave no recovery point (a lost mount, a cleared directory). 26 rather than 24 so an ordinary late dump does not page. ⛔ Must be POSITIVE — zero is refused at startup, because every dump is older than zero hours the instant it is written, so it would page every morning on a healthy system until someone muted it. There is no upper bound, but setting it far above your dump cadence silently widens the blind spot: at 720 a 29-day-old dump still reads healthy. To switch the watchdog off use BACKUP_ENABLED=false.

Config.Name: BACKUP_FRESHNESS_CRON
Config.Description: When that disk check runs, as a 5-field cron expression in SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE. Morning by design: it reports on the night that has already happened, to someone awake to act on it. ⚠️ If you restrict the day-of-week use a NAME (sun, mon-fri) — the scheduler counts days from MONDAY, so a numeric 0 means Monday, not Sunday, and that off-by-one has cost this system real data twice.

Config.Name: VACUUM_ENABLED
Config.Description: Nightly VACUUM (ANALYZE). Cheap, and it keeps the query planner's statistics fresh after each night of ingestion — read performance degrades without it.

Config.Name: VACUUM_CRON
Config.Description: When the nightly VACUUM runs (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). Keep it clear of BACKUP_TIME so the two do not contend for the same disk. Use NAMED days if you restrict the day-of-week.

Config.Name: ORPHAN_SCAN_ENABLED
Config.Description: Scan for compressed chunk relations orphaned by a dropped hypertable, alongside the nightly VACUUM. DETECTION ONLY — it reports, it never drops anything, because dropping stored data is a deliberate admin action and not a timer's decision.

Config.Name: B2_BUCKET
Config.Description: LEAVE BLANK unless this container is genuinely the thing doing your offsite copy. The built-in Backblaze B2 leg uploads each dump whole (no deduplication) and holds the B2 credentials in this container. If a separate snapshot/backup tool already reads BACKUP_DIR and pushes offsite, enabling this as well double-pushes the same data and puts a second copy of the key on this host. All of bucket/key-id/application-key/endpoint are required together to enable it; any blank means land-to-disk only, which is the intended posture.

Config.Name: B2_KEY_ID
Config.Description: Backblaze B2 key id, for the optional built-in offsite leg. See B2_BUCKET — normally blank.

Config.Name: B2_APPLICATION_KEY
Config.Description: Backblaze B2 application key, for the optional built-in offsite leg. See B2_BUCKET — normally blank.

Config.Name: B2_ENDPOINT_URL
Config.Description: Backblaze B2 S3-compatible endpoint, e.g. https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com. See B2_BUCKET — normally blank.

Config.Name: B2_PREFIX
Config.Description: Key prefix (folder) within the B2 bucket. Blank is a VALUE here rather than a request for the default — it means the bucket root, which is a legitimate choice. Only consulted when the B2 leg is enabled.

Config.Name: SCHEDULER_ENABLED
Config.Description: Master switch for ALL recurring work — the daily cycle, every feed, the backups, and every watchdog. False leaves the API serving reads while nothing maintains the warehouse; useful for a second read-only instance, dangerous as a default.

Config.Name: SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE
Config.Description: The timezone every MARKET job runs in. Eastern by definition, not by preference: NAV publication times, the close, and the settlement windows are all defined by the exchange session, so changing this misaligns the jobs with the market they follow. The nightly backup is deliberately NOT on this clock — see BACKUP_TIMEZONE. Must be a full IANA zone name; a blank falls back to the default rather than taking the scheduler down.

Config.Name: DAILY_CYCLE_CRON
Config.Description: The main maintenance cycle (ingest, materialize, sponsor refresh, analyze, resolve), 5-field cron in SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE. Closed-end fund NAVs publish around 18:45 Eastern, so a morning run would ingest yesterday's numbers. Non-trading days are skipped by the cycle itself. Use NAMED days if you restrict the day-of-week.

Config.Name: HEARTBEAT_ENABLED
Config.Description: The alert-on-SILENCE watchdog: it notices when a scheduled job has simply stopped reporting, as opposed to reporting a failure. This exists because a dead feed once went unnoticed for two weeks — a job that fails is loud, a job that stops running is silent. Leave it on.

Config.Name: HEARTBEAT_CRON
Config.Description: How often that silence check runs (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). Every 4 hours EVERY day, including weekends — a feed that dies on a Friday evening should not wait until Monday to be reported. The check is cheap and the alert is edge-triggered, so a genuinely dead feed still only pages about once a day.

Config.Name: FRED_API_KEY
Config.Description: FRED (St. Louis Fed) API key — free from fred.stlouisfed.org (32 alphanumeric). Enables the macro feed (yield curve, rates, spreads, inflation, dollar index). Unset = the FRED job no-ops; the rest of Tape is unaffected.

Config.Name: FRED_ENABLED
Config.Description: Whether the macro feed runs at all. With no API key above it no-ops regardless — it never fabricates a series.

Config.Name: FRED_CRON
Config.Description: When the macro pull runs (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). Weekdays after the FRED daily update window — rates post around 16:15 Eastern. The write is an idempotent upsert, so a missed run simply self-heals on the next one.

Config.Name: SEC_USER_AGENT
Config.Description: REQUIRED for SEC/EDGAR access: a compliant contact in the form 'Name email@domain' (e.g. 'Your Name you@your-domain.example'). SEC fair-access asks every automated client to identify itself and stay contactable. Blank falls back to a repository-URL User-Agent that SEC now 403s, which takes out the fundamentals and corporate-actions feeds — the container still starts and the failure appears later, at whatever hour those timers fire, so Tape logs a WARNING at boot when this is unset. The image carries no default on purpose: a contact address is personal, and baking one into a public image would publish it.

Config.Name: FUNDAMENTALS_ENABLED
Config.Description: The SEC EDGAR XBRL fundamentals feed — free, keyless, and on its own rate limiter, so it does not compete with the market-data budget. Needs SEC_USER_AGENT set.

Config.Name: FUNDAMENTALS_CRON
Config.Description: When the weekly fundamentals refresh runs (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). Filings land on a quarterly rhythm, so weekly is ample; the upsert is idempotent and a missed run self-heals. Use NAMED days — sun, not 0.

Config.Name: FUNDAMENTALS_GAP_OVERDUE_DAYS
Config.Description: A filer whose latest periodic filing is older than this is flagged as overdue. One quarter (about 91 days) plus the roughly 40-day filing lag, plus a little slack.

Config.Name: FUNDAMENTALS_ACTIVE_FILER_DAYS
Config.Description: A filing within this window marks a symbol as an ACTIVE filer, which blocks the price-history machinery from writing it off as delisted — investigate rather than lock out. About 15 months, so an annual-only filer plus its filing lag still counts as alive.

Config.Name: EDGAR_RECHECK_DAYS
Config.Description: How long to cache the SEC lifecycle-filing check (deregistrations, mergers). That paperwork moves on a scale of weeks, so re-probing daily meant a full EDGAR sweep every day for nothing. Zero probes every run.

Config.Name: DISTRIBUTIONS_ENABLED
Config.Description: Closed-end fund distribution history. One call per fund with no bulk endpoint, hence the weekly cadence below.

Config.Name: DISTRIBUTIONS_CRON
Config.Description: When the weekly distribution refresh runs (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). Idempotent upsert; a missed run self-heals next week. Use NAMED days — sun, not 0.

Config.Name: DIVIDENDS_ENABLED
Config.Description: Dividend capture. The upstream exposes only the current and next dividend with no history, so this accrues forward — every day it does not run is history that cannot be recovered later.

Config.Name: DIVIDENDS_CRON
Config.Description: When dividend capture runs (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). Weekdays after the close. Use NAMED days.

Config.Name: UNIVERSE_ENABLED
Config.Description: Weekly refresh of the instrument universe from the public listing directories. The upsert never deletes, so a delisted symbol keeps its history rather than vanishing from the record.

Config.Name: UNIVERSE_CRON
Config.Description: When the universe refresh runs (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). Listings change on listing events rather than intraday, so weekly is ample. Use NAMED days — sun, not 0.

Config.Name: EOD_SWEEP_ENABLED
Config.Description: The universe-wide end-of-day capture. Without it a session only gets bars for symbols somebody happened to request — measured once at 2 bars for a session against the roughly 12,400 a normal one produces.

Config.Name: EOD_SWEEP_CRON
Config.Description: When that sweep runs (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). Just after the close; the only precondition is that the session has ended. Use NAMED days.

Config.Name: EOD_SWEEP_MAX_SYMBOLS
Config.Description: Cap on symbols per sweep. ZERO MEANS UNBOUNDED and is the production setting — one daily bar per symbol is affordable at the measured read rate. The knob exists for small smoke runs.

Config.Name: EOD_SWEEP_LOOKBACK_DAYS
Config.Description: How recently a symbol must have traded to be swept. Tens of thousands of symbols have a bar in the last month but only about 12,400 print on a given session — the rest are sparse or delisted, and sweeping them spends budget confirming a dead symbol is still dead. A symbol that resumes trading re-enters on its own.

Config.Name: EOD_PROVISIONAL_ENABLED
Config.Description: Fill today's bar provisionally from an alternate source while waiting for the official daily candle, which the primary feed publishes hours after the close. Turning this off does not make the history wrong — it makes it a session late.

Config.Name: EOD_FILL_COALESCE_SEC
Config.Description: Minimum gap between fill attempts for the same symbol and session, whatever the outcome. The history endpoint is consumer-facing, so this is what stops a watchlist refresh turning into an upstream storm.

Config.Name: EOD_RECONCILE_CRON
Config.Description: When provisional bars are reconciled against the official candle (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). The upstream does not document what hour it publishes, so this polls across the evening rather than guessing a single time. ⚠️ The window RUNS PAST MIDNIGHT and covers EVERY day, both deliberately: a weekday-only window would leave a Friday session's candle — which lands early Saturday — unreconciled until Monday.

Config.Name: EOD_RECONCILE_PROBE_LIMIT
Config.Description: Each reconcile pass first re-probes this many newest bars. If none of them have settled the upstream has not published yet and the pass stops there, which is what stops a dozen nightly passes from re-probing twelve thousand bars each. Sampling the newest is valid because they are all from the same session.

Config.Name: EOD_RECONCILE_POLL_LIMIT
Config.Description: The real drain, once the probe proves the candle is landing. Across the post-midnight passes this must exceed one session's production (roughly 12,400) or the backlog compounds nightly.

Config.Name: EOD_RECONCILE_LIMIT
Config.Description: Upper bound on how many provisional bars a single reconcile pass inside the daily cycle will try to settle.

Config.Name: EOD_WATCHDOG_ENABLED
Config.Description: Watchdog for provisional bars that survived into a later session — at that point it is an anomaly, not a bar.

Config.Name: EOD_WATCHDOG_CRON
Config.Description: When that watchdog runs (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). Weekday mid-morning, by which point the prior session's official candle should exist. Use NAMED days.

Config.Name: INTRADAY_ENABLED
Config.Description: Scheduled intraday bar capture. Before this existed, intraday bars accumulated only as a side effect of somebody hitting an endpoint, so the minute series that alerting is meant to read did not really exist.

Config.Name: INTRADAY_CRON
Config.Description: When intraday capture runs (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). Shortly after the close: a session's MINUTE data is complete the moment the bell rings, unlike the daily candle. Use NAMED days.

Config.Name: INTRADAY_MAX_SYMBOLS
Config.Description: How many symbols get intraday capture. This is bounded by CALL BUDGET, not by the size of the universe: one minute-history pull per symbol per session across the whole instrument table would be tens of thousands of calls a day, against a budget that belongs to the backfill queue. So the intraday universe is an explicit bounded selection rather than everything.

Config.Name: INTRADAY_SYMBOLS
Config.Description: Comma-separated symbols to ALWAYS include in intraday capture, ahead of any automatic selection — the deterministic core of what this deployment actually watches. Blank is fine and means the selection is entirely automatic.

Config.Name: INTRADAY_1M_RETENTION_DAYS
Config.Description: How long 1-minute bars are kept. By far the largest lane, and the substrate alerting is built on. ⚠️ Past this horizon the data is GONE and the upstream will not re-serve it — this warehouse is the only source of record for old minute data.

Config.Name: INTRADAY_BASE_RETENTION_DAYS
Config.Description: How long the 30-minute bars are kept. Longer than the 1-minute lane because they are the resample base for the hourly and 4-hourly series and are roughly thirty times cheaper per session.

Config.Name: INTRADAY_EXTENDED_HOURS
Config.Description: Capture pre-market and after-hours bars as well. Stored ADDITIVELY and session-tagged, never folded into the regular bars — the regular series reads identically whether this is on or off. Off by default because thin pre/post prints whipsaw the indicators built on top of them.

Config.Name: INTRADAY_PACING_SECONDS
Config.Description: Delay between per-symbol intraday pulls, so a several-hundred-symbol sweep is a paced drain rather than a burst against the same limiter the live quote path shares.

Config.Name: BACKFILL_ENABLED
Config.Description: The overnight drain of the repair/backfill queue. This is what actually closes the holes that gap detection finds.

Config.Name: BACKFILL_CRON
Config.Description: When the drain starts (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). After the evening jobs and hours before the open. Use NAMED days if you restrict the day-of-week.

Config.Name: BACKFILL_NIGHTLY_CALLS
Config.Description: Upstream calls the drain may spend in one night. This governs how much it is willing to SPEND, not how fast — the rate limit below is what governs speed, and the adaptive limiter backs everything off the moment the upstream pushes back.

Config.Name: BACKFILL_MAX_SECONDS
Config.Description: Hard wall-clock stop for one drain. Six hours, checked in the drain loop AND inside each job, so a run can never straddle the market open however much budget is left.

Config.Name: BACKFILL_CONCURRENCY
Config.Description: How many workers drain the queue at once. A single worker is latency-bound and cannot exceed roughly 150 calls a minute however high the rate limit goes, so this is the only lever that moves throughput. Safety does not come from this number: all workers share ONE rate governor, so a single rejection backs every worker off together. It is also tunable at runtime via the admin API without a redeploy. ⚠️ Do not raise it past what DB_POOL_SIZE serves — each worker holds a connection across its calls.

Config.Name: BACKFILL_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
Config.Description: Ceiling on any ONE queued job. A worker slot is scarce during a parallel drain, so a wedged job costs a share of the whole night until it clears. Ten minutes is far above any healthy job and far below a lost night.

Config.Name: SELFHEAL_ENABLED
Config.Description: The nightly sweep that DETECTS missing daily bars and queues repairs for the drain. Turning it off does not break anything immediately — it just stops the warehouse noticing and closing its own holes.

Config.Name: SELFHEAL_CRON
Config.Description: When that sweep runs (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). Deliberately 30 minutes AHEAD of the backfill drain, so what it queues is drained the same night and the loop closes in one cycle instead of two.

Config.Name: SELFHEAL_DETECT_LIMIT
Config.Description: Cap on symbols the sweep re-examines per run. Detection touches only the database, so this bounds DB time and not upstream traffic. Set above the live candidate population so a single night reaches all of it — it is a safety valve, not a ration.

Config.Name: SELFHEAL_EDGE_LIMIT
Config.Description: Cap on symbols the sweep may ENQUEUE per run — the throttle that actually matters, since this is the stage that creates upstream work. It still cannot cause a rate storm: the drain spends the calls, under its own budget and deadline.

Config.Name: ALTFILL_ENABLED
Config.Description: Whether a missing daily bar the primary feed has DECLINED (asked, answered empty, no error) is repaired from an alternate source in the same run and stored with its origin recorded. Set false to keep detecting and reporting such holes without filling them — the self-heal loop still runs, it just stops closing on its own. A bar is never filled from an alternate when the primary feed FAILED, so a feed outage can never be masked by this.

Config.Name: ALTFILL_MAX_WINDOW_DAYS
Config.Description: Widest repair window the alternate lane will attempt in one pass. A normal repair is a session to a few weeks; a multi-year window is a deep-history walk that came back empty, and asking a free keyless third party to serve one is neither polite nor likely to work. Wider windows are left to the primary feed.

Config.Name: TIINGO_API_TOKEN
Config.Description: OPTIONAL personal API token for the higher-quality alternate price source (free tier at tiingo.com). Tape repairs a missing daily bar from alternate sources when the primary feed is asked for that session and returns nothing; two keyless sources are tried first, and this one is tried only for what they could not serve, so a personal quota is spent on the remainder rather than the whole universe. Leave BLANK and that lane is completely dormant — no request is made, nothing is logged, and the free lanes do all the work. Unset is a fully supported configuration, not a degraded one.

Config.Name: GAP_LANES_ENABLED
Config.Description: Gap detection for the non-price lanes (intraday, macro, corporate actions). These had detectors and tests but no timer, so in practice nothing ever judged them.

Config.Name: GAP_LANES_DAILY_CRON
Config.Description: When the intraday gap check runs (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). After intraday capture, so a run cannot overlap the capture it is judging. Use NAMED days — the numbered form here once ran Tuesday to Saturday and cost every Monday's minute data permanently.

Config.Name: GAP_LANES_WEEKLY_CRON
Config.Description: When the macro and corporate-actions gap checks run (5-field cron, SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE). Both judge a series against its own measured rhythm — monthly inflation prints, quarterly dividends — so a daily pass would re-derive the same answer six extra times a week. Use NAMED days — sun, not 0.

Config.Name: SCHWAB_RATE_PER_MIN
Config.Description: Total upstream read budget per minute, across every lane. Set against a MEASURED ceiling rather than a documented one: the upstream publishes no rate-limit headers and no retry hint, and rejections were first observed starting around 790 calls a minute, with 705 sustained cleanly. 750 sits below that wall. Also tunable at runtime through the admin API.

Config.Name: SCHWAB_BULK_RATE_PER_MIN
Config.Description: The slice of the budget above that background and bulk work may use, leaving the remainder as guaranteed headroom for live requests. ⚠️ MUST STAY BELOW SCHWAB_RATE_PER_MIN — a reserve larger than the total would let bulk work consume everything and leave interactive callers no guaranteed share. The runtime admin knob refuses that inversion, but nothing validates it at STARTUP, so a value set here is applied as written — get it right in this field.

Config.Name: AGG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS
Config.Description: How long the daily aggregate summaries are memoized. The daily cycle invalidates them explicitly, so this only bounds drift from out-of-band writes.

Config.Name: CLIENT_REGISTRY_ENABLED
Config.Description: THE AUTH SWITCH — opt-in enforcement of the per-service client registry. true = callers must present X-Client-Id + X-Client-Secret, the secret is argon2-verified, and the scope the path requires is enforced — bar a small frozen set of paths that no caller can hold a credential for (the OAuth login and redirect), which stay open in every mode by design. false is the CODE default and is NOT a safe setting to leave alone: it falls back to a shared legacy key, and when no such key is configured — which is the case for a container created from this template, because the legacy key below is blank by default — Tape serves every API endpoint, market data and operator alike, to anyone who can reach it. (The browsable /admin/docs pages are the one exception: those stay closed unless the CF_ACCESS_* pair below is set.) Seeding client rows does NOT switch enforcement on; this flag is the single switch, so the cutover stays explicit and reversible. Seed your clients, then set this true on any deployment reachable by anything but you.

Config.Name: TRUSTED_HOSTS
Config.Description: Host-header allowlist. A request whose Host header is not on this list is answered 400 before any routing happens, which closes an open-redirect in the framework's trailing-slash handling (an unlisted Host could otherwise steer an unauthenticated 307 — method, body and credential headers preserved — to an arbitrary origin). Comma-separated hostnames; the port is stripped before matching, and *.example.com wildcards are accepted. The shipped default admits ONLY the container's own loopback (which is what the built-in healthcheck uses), so you MUST add every name and IP your callers actually use — the server's LAN IP, any reverse-proxy hostname that forwards the original Host — or those callers will receive 400s while the container itself still reports healthy. A single * disables Host validation entirely and re-opens the redirect; it exists only as an explicit, visible opt-out.

Config.Name: TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT
Config.Description: How many reverse proxies sit in front of Tape, for the client-IP allowlist's X-Forwarded-For parse. The genuine client IP is read as the Nth entry FROM THE RIGHT of the XFF chain, so values a caller injected — which sit to the LEFT of whatever a trusted proxy appends — are not selected. 1 = a single reverse proxy in front (e.g. Nginx Proxy Manager); set 2 if an edge proxy such as Cloudflare also fronts the request; 0 disables XFF trust entirely and uses the direct peer only. Set this to the number of proxies you actually run, and NEVER higher: counting more hops than exist reaches past the trusted tail into the part of the chain the CALLER supplied, which is the half an attacker can forge. Counting too few is merely useless, never unsafe — it reads an inner proxy's own address. Two caveats worth knowing: counting from the right only holds while every request really does traverse those proxies, so if this container's port is reachable directly the tail can still be forged — treat the IP allowlist as a second factor behind the client secret, never a sole gate; and this setting is consulted ONLY when CLIENT_REGISTRY_ENABLED is true, so at the defaults shipped here it does nothing.

Config.Name: TAPE_API_KEYS
Config.Description: LEGACY shared-key auth, superseded by the client registry above and offered here only so an existing deployment can be read and retired. Comma-separated keys; when set, market endpoints require a matching X-API-Key header. Leave BLANK and use CLIENT_REGISTRY_ENABLED instead — a shared key cannot express scopes, so every holder gets the operator surface too.

Config.Name: AUTH_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS
Config.Description: How long a successfully verified credential is served from memory before it must be re-verified. Rotating, revoking or editing a client invalidates its entry immediately, so this only bounds drift from changes made directly in the database.

Config.Name: AUTH_LAST_USED_FLUSH_SECONDS
Config.Description: How often the batched last-used timestamps are written to the database. Deliberately approximate — the write is kept off the request hot path.

Config.Name: AUTH_FAILURE_MAX
Config.Description: Credential failures from one source IP within the window below before further attempts are refused BEFORE any password hashing happens. Only successful verifications are cached — caching failures would leak which client ids exist, by timing — so the wrong-secret path otherwise pays the full hashing cost every time, unauthenticated. Zero disables the throttle. There is no lockout state: a client that fixes its secret is served as soon as its failures age out.

Config.Name: AUTH_FAILURE_WINDOW_SECONDS
Config.Description: The sliding window for the failure count above.

Config.Name: CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN
Config.Description: Cloudflare Access team hostname, no scheme (e.g. <team>.cloudflareaccess.com). Enables the BROWSABLE operator docs at /admin/docs, which are gated by an Access application covering /admin/* on this host. Leave blank and /admin/* returns 503 — unconfigured is CLOSED.

Config.Name: CF_ACCESS_AUD
Config.Description: The Access application's Application Audience (AUD) tag. Must be THIS application's tag: the same team signs every other Access app's tokens with the same key, and aud is the only claim that separates them. Required alongside CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN for /admin/docs.

Config.Name: LOG_LEVEL
Config.Description: Application log level: debug, info, warning, error. debug is genuinely verbose on a warehouse this size — useful for a specific investigation, not as a resting state.
